Theme

number card noun

the two to the ten of a suit

also deuce, pip card, spot card, two of hearts, seven of diamonds, ten of clubs

Renaissance

M-O s.v. card ranks, from Vives 1540
Andresian p. 16

dyas, dyadis f.

noun, third declension

the two

Vives’s name for the card (M-O s.v. card ranks). In Lewis & Short the number two (Macr., Aug.). Vives names the cards from two to ten with the Greek number nouns, but four and six with the Latin names of throws at dice.

Other words

  • trias, triadis f. — the three

    noun, third declension · Renaissance · M-O s.v. card ranks; Andresian p. 16

    The number three, a triad (Mart. Cap.).

  • quaterniō, quaterniōnis m. — the four

    noun, third declension · Renaissance · M-O s.v. card ranks; Andresian p. 16

    The number four (Mart. Cap.); the four at dice (Isid. Orig. 18.65).

  • pentas, pentadis f. — the five

    noun, third declension · Renaissance · M-O s.v. card ranks; Andresian p. 16

    The number five (Mart. Cap.).

  • sēniō, sēniōnis m. — the six

    noun, third declension · Renaissance · M-O s.v. card ranks; Andresian p. 16

    Classically the six at dice (Pers. 3.48; Aug. ap. Suet. Aug. 71); see number on a die.

  • heptas, heptadis f. — the seven

    noun, third declension · Renaissance · M-O s.v. card ranks; Andresian p. 16

    The number seven (Mart. Cap.).

  • ogdoas, ogdoadis f. — the eight

    noun, third declension · Renaissance · M-O s.v. card ranks; Andresian p. 16

  • enneas, enneadis f. — the nine

    noun, third declension · Renaissance · M-O s.v. card ranks; Andresian p. 16

    The number nine (Censorinus, Mart. Cap.).

  • decas, decadis f. — the ten

    noun, third declension · Renaissance · M-O s.v. card ranks; Andresian p. 16

    A decade, a set of ten (Tert., Mart. Cap.). With the suit in the genitive: decas cordium, the ten of hearts.
